claimed.text: Justice said the ADAM specimens' structure and composition are not from any known military or commercial application, while conceding they came from sources with varying levels of chain-of-custody documentation.

How the samples reached TTSA matters: Linda Moulton Howe says they were tested by Carnegie Science's Department of Terrestrial Magnetism in 1996 and by Puthoff on several occasions, and the board traces the chain from an anonymous source to Art Bell, to Howe, to TTSA for $35,000, to the Army agreement.

Kari DeLonge told The Intercept that Elizondo took over AATIP in 2010 as Director, and TTSA's History series Unidentified, executive produced by Tom DeLonge, portrayed him as having led it for eight years.
Mellon says he received the three Navy videos from a Defense Department official in the Pentagon parking lot and gave them to the New York Times; the official has never been identified.

Podesta called for declassification of UFO records at the National Press Club in October 2002, and on leaving the White House in 2015 said his biggest failure was not securing disclosure of the UFO files.

An Army spokesman said that because the Army's interest is in novel materials, speculation about their origin is immaterial, and that it does not release details of collaborative work until the work has concluded.
McCasland was reported missing from his Albuquerque home in February 2026, and Rep. Burlison's staff had been trying to reach him for a separate congressional inquiry.

contested.text: Oak Ridge assessed the specimen as terrestrial in origin and found it does not meet the theoretical requirements to work as a terahertz waveguide, while AARO notes that its undocumented chain of custody and conflicting accounts leave its origin unclear. Puthoff had already written in 2012 that testing produced no anomalous outcome.

No technical output, characterisation or Army finding from the CRADA has been published, and the records disagree on its length: the released text gives a term to 30 September 2023, while other accounts describe a five-year agreement entered on 17 October 2019.

TTSA hosted and distributed the three Navy videos from 2017, framing them as officially cleared, a framing the Navy contested in September 2019, when its spokesman said neither the cognizant Navy offices nor DOPSR had any record of a request for unrestricted release of the videos in 2017.

The Podesta release establishes only that DeLonge made the Roswell and Wright-Patterson assertion in writing, not that it happened, and the identification of the email's general with William Neil McCasland rests on the name and his biography, not on the email.

A later account that the Podesta emails carried a Prometheus framing and Linda Moulton Howe material does not survive a search: neither appears in the release, and the speaker who reported it said he was relaying Peter Levenda rather than quoting anything.

Other voices decline to corroborate the McCasland story: Jeremy Corbell called the reported McCasland-DeLonge contact part of an operation, and former Army remote viewer Lyn Buchanan said he knew nothing of him.

The Intercept reported that TTSA's own filings describe it as a motion picture and video tape production concern, and that DeLonge's role as executive producer of Unidentified, featuring Elizondo and Mellon, was not disclosed on screen.

The board reads ADAM's value as custodial and legal rather than scientific, a private chain of custody that let claimed exotic material reach an Army laboratory under an unclassified instrument, and infers from the seven days between Elizondo's resignation and the launch that the company was assembled before he left.

lead.text: To The Stars Academy was a Delaware public benefit corporation founded in 2017 with Tom DeLonge, Jim Semivan and Harold Puthoff as directors. It hired the former Pentagon official Luis Elizondo, bought pieces of metal it said came from craft of unknown origin, and in October 2019 signed a research agreement with an Army vehicle laboratory over them.

record.text: TTSA's SEC filings list Kari DeLonge as Chief Content Officer with $100,000 cash compensation for FY2017 and options on five million shares valued at about $18.96 million; a July 2020 offering exhibit valued the company at $65 million and described ADAM and the Army agreement.
At the launch Elizondo was described as former Director of Programs investigating Unidentified Aerial Threats for the Office of the Secretary of Defense.

A September 2018 filing recorded that TTSA was preparing research into materials relevant to its plans in space-time metric engineering, having partnered with EarthTech in August 2018, and the offering materials say some specimens had been in documented possession since the mid-1990s.

The CRADA, filed with the SEC as Exhibit 6.28, is titled Novel and Emerging Technology Exploitation and names Bean Soave and Joseph Cannon as government principal investigators. Its research areas are inertial mass reduction, structural and electromagnetic metamaterials, quantum physics and communications and beamed energy propulsion, with TTSA's in-kind contribution valued at about $1 million and a term to 30 September 2023.

Cannon was quoted calling TTSA an exciting, non-traditional source for novel materials. On 21 February 2020 the Army withheld in full 29 emails, 100 pages, of his TTSA correspondence under FOIA exemptions (b)(4) and (b)(5).

AARO states that the organisation owning the alleged crash material negotiated an agreement with the Army in 2019 to analyse the samples, and that AARO later acquired the specimen with stakeholder permission and contracted Oak Ridge in 2022 to test it.

DeLonge wrote to Podesta on 25 January 2016 that the Roswell material had been shipped to the laboratory at Wright-Patterson and that General McCasland had run that laboratory until a couple of years earlier, that he had worked with the general for four months and that the general helped assemble his advisory team. The meeting thread runs through an address signing Neil McC and copies Rob Weiss of Lockheed Martin.
On 22 February 2016 DeLonge wrote to Podesta that Mr. Weiss from Lockheed's Skunk Works had asked him for any updates.

McCasland's Air Force biography records him as Commander of the Air Force Research Laboratory at Wright-Patterson and, from 2009 to 2011, Director of Special Programs in the acquisition Under Secretary's office, which is not the intelligence office that handled the AAWSAP special access request.

The Clinton White House's UFO FOIA collections are external correspondence rather than programme records. In March 2015 Bob Fish wrote to Podesta that the Air Force's DSP satellite programme collects hard data on UFOs, while conceding he was never fully briefed into it; Podesta's reply was non-committal.
DoD authorised release of the three Navy videos TTSA had circulated on 27 April 2020, saying the phenomena in them remain characterised as unidentified.

summary.text: The company launched publicly on 11 October 2017 with Science, Aerospace and Entertainment divisions; a DeLonge family trust entity held 60 million of its 70 million Class A shares. By April 2018 it had raised about $1.09 million of a $50 million offering, against an FY2017 net loss of $30.7 million, most of it stock-based compensation.

Its people came from government and industry: Elizondo as Director of Global Security and Special Programs, Christopher Mellon, a former Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense for Intelligence, as adviser, Steve Justice after 31 years at Lockheed's Skunk Works, and Semivan after 25 years in the CIA's Directorate of Operations.

Its ADAM project set out to acquire and analyse samples from advanced aerospace vehicles of unknown origin with Puthoff's EarthTech International, and SEC filings record a $35,000 payment for items including six pieces of bismuth and magnesium-zinc metal and a piece of aluminium.

CRADA 19-15 with the Army's Ground Vehicle Systems Center at Detroit Arsenal was signed on 10 October 2019 by the Center's director Jeffery Langhout and TTSA's Chief Content Officer Kari DeLonge, with Elizondo as TTSA's principal investigator.

The company's pre-history runs through DeLonge's 2016 emails to John Podesta about a General McCasland, and its afterlife through the specimen, which by AARO's account passed through the Army to AARO and Oak Ridge.
